geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
This assessment covers G.QP.4, G.T.1c, G.GF.7, G.QP.2 (coordinate). Use the targets below as a checklist: can you do each one without notes?

  • 7.1 I can state area postulates (congruence, addition).
  • 7.2 I can derive and use rectangle and square area.
  • 7.3 I can derive triangle area from rectangles: a right triangle is half a rectangle, and any triangle is a sum or difference of right triangles.
  • 7.4 I can derive parallelogram and trapezoid area by splitting them into triangles.
  • 7.5 I can find areas of composite and irregular polygons.
  • 7.6 I can prove the Pythagorean Theorem by rearranging areas.
  • 7.7 I can use the converse to classify triangles and see the theorem in a Pythagoras tree.
  • 7.9 I can derive the distance formula from the Pythagorean Theorem.
  • 7.10 I can find perimeters and areas of polygons from coordinates.
  • 7.11 I can prove a quadrilateral is a rhombus, rectangle, or square on the coordinate plane.
  • 7.12 I can choose a convenient coordinate setup to prove a general result.

slides.title: Practice: 7.1
slides.html: Two figures have equal areas. Must they be congruent?
slides.reveal: No. A 2 by 8 rectangle and a 4 by 4 square both have area 16.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • area and perimeter grow together
  • height is always a side
  • a² + b² = c² works for any triangle
  • distance formula is unrelated to Pythagoras
